utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-33-A, the Prosecutor versus Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Appearance for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Norman Farrell with Mr. Mathias Marcussen and Wolfgang Sakulin for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farrell. For the appellant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence will be represented as it has been the case so far, by myself, Nenad Petrusic, and my colleague Mr. Tomislav Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrusic. General Krstic, there is no need to stand up, but can you hear the proceedings in a language which you can understand? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sit down, please. This is a Status Conference held in accordance with the requirements of Rule 65 bis. Before we get to the state of the pleadings and motions and responses and replies, is there anything you wish to raise, Mr. Farrell?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Nothing on behalf of the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: How about you, Mr. Petrusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing on behalf of the Defence either, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, now, subject to the outstanding matters for which there are some additional material to be filed by the Prosecution, it seems the pleadings are closed in the appeal. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: In terms of the general pleadings, yes. In terms of any evidence filed by the Defence in support of their, yes, other matters, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, there's a particular motion that we want to dispose of. That's the motion by the appellant for the disclosure of ex parte communications. That was filed the 6th of March, and the Prosecution response on the 22nd of March. Is there going to be a reply filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're currently talking to the Prosecution regarding just a small quantity of additional material that we believe the Prosecutor can provide to us, and we will proceed in two manners; either we will withdraw our request, our motion, or cut it down to the contested quantity of the material. The situation, as I see it now, without prior consultation with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We want to make clear, Mr. Visnjic, what we're speaking about. I'm not talking about Rule 68 material at the moment. I'm talking about your motion for disclosure of all ex parte communications because of the disclosure by the Prosecution that they'd had these two ex parte meetings with the Trial Chamber. Now, is there going to be a reply filed by the appellant in relation to that motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is a possibility for us to withdraw our request for disclosure if a minor detail can be clarified with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In relation to the ex parte communications, with the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in relation to the ex parte communications.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, that will save some work. Now, in relation -- thank you very much. Now, in relation to the Rule 68 material, Mr. Farrell, the response, if that's the correct terminology -- I think we've quite lost the right terminology here. But the riposte by the appellant to your explanation about the Rule 68 material has raised a number of issues. Are you going to respond in some way to that, or are you going to deal with it in a supplementary response brief?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: To be frank, we were actually discussing that earlier today. There are some issues, as you've identified, which are not the subject actually of the original response and motion. We were going to address one or two issues. It --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is -- if I may say so, some important issues have been raised, and it may become necessary for us to have to consider them in the appeal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: In relation to the final reply by my colleagues, my learned colleagues the Defence, in relation to a couple of the matters, we certainly would like to address them because they are, in our view, somewhat new in that document. Some of the others we'll consider whether it's appropriate to or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may be that this will be an appeal on which we'll have to give some thought to how Rule 68 should really be interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I think in fact the -- some of the issues we've placed before you for that reason, Your Honour, especially the determination of what constitutes Rule 68 evidence, as there is dispute between the parties. Obviously at some point in time, guidance would assist, both in relation to this appeal but in relation to the work we are engaging on a regular basis. So if it would assist, I'd ask also to try to put the Prosecution's best position forward. We will take, with the leave of the Chamber, of course, the opportunity to respond to a few of the matters that may be raised in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be a very good idea if you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: And while we're about it - it may not be in this particular case - but we seem to have a terminology problem about responses and respondent's briefs. Once we're into the -- once we're into the appeal, you have to file briefs. And it seems to have become a habit that you are asking for leave to file a further response, or even worse - I suppose it comes from America if not Canada - a supplemental document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's fair enough. The -- I think, though - I am certainly open to correction - that with respect to the appellant's brief and the two filings by the Prosecution with respect to the respondent's brief, we were -- they were called respondent's briefs because there was our response brief and then our supplementary response brief. On the responses to their motions, which include the motion for production, we didn't put briefs because they were responses to motions in fact. But I may be wrong in that regard. But that's the manner in which I proceeded on the definitional terminological --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It may be it was -- in Kordic -- I'm not sure. I signed an order this morning in which I drew attention to the difference between a supplemental response and a supplementary respondent's brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: If I can, simply for the benefit of the Prosecution, clarify the practice we have been following, or I must say I had been following, was that when it dealt with under Rule 111, it was a brief; when it dealt with all motions, it was a response to their motion. If that has not been filed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down for the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: My apologies to the interpreters. If that practice has not been followed either in the Krstic case or in the Kordic case, I'll ensure that we have some consistency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It would certainly make it easier. All right. Then, well, how long would you like in order for you to reply to this material put forward by the appellant?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I don't think there's any problem with between seven and ten days, the normal time period. Ten days is the normal time period. We've had it for a while. We can do it within seven to ten days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think you've had it for more than seven days. It's dated the 26th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: So anyway, if you can get it in by early next week. Let's say Wednesday. What's Wednesday? That would be the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The 10th of April. And Mr. Visnjic, how long do you think you'll need in order to get your reply to the ex parte communications if you were going to file one?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Also about ten days, depending, of course, on the response of the Prosecution. And I will discuss this problem with Mr. Farrell today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You've already had ten days. Do you want another ten days? I don't mind. I just want to have in my diary when to expect the document, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, another ten days, if possible, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: All right. The 15th of April for the appellant to reply on the motion for disclosure of ex parte communications. There has been a problem about ex parte communications. I've been trying to persuade the Prosecution not to come along ex parte to get documents signed. I have written about it in two decisions now at Trial Chamber level, and one day I'm going to make sure that I say the same thing here because it's an unfortunate impression which is conveyed that when parties come along trying to get things done, perhaps for matters of speed but, nevertheless, they're not being done in public. Now, anything else we can deal with? The hearing of this appeal is sliding down slightly. There's been a problem, I gather, in relation to a -- an appeal which has been heard, and they're trying to get the judgement out. So you may be finding that we'll be about a month later than originally expected. But it will be about the middle of the year sometime by the look of it, or just shortly after the middle of the year. That depends, of course, upon the Rule 115. And for that, we're waiting until you've responded -- I'm sorry, you've sorted out between yourselves the material that has been disclosed. And at that stage, I think somebody better ask for the matter to be listed so we can sort out another timetable. It may be you can do it between yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Just for your information, if it may assist in any way, as of yesterday, the -- there's -- as you know from the motion for production and the agreement between the Defence and the Prosecution, there are intercepts that were to be disclosed. As of yesterday, the final four hard-copy versions of the handwritten notes of the intercepts, the CDs, which are the searchable ones in relation to ones that we've actually scanned and have in CD form, which are 106; then there's the additional four hard-copy ones which we don't have in searchable form, so they weren't included in the CD; and the remainder of any statements were provided to the Defence as of yesterday, when they arrived. We asked that they be given to them when they appear because of the confidential nature of some of the documents. We have requested from the Defence that they return any documents which are either of our concern because of their confidential nature or because they're evidence in the case, that they be returned within 60 days. So in fairness to the Defence, that's the time frame we've asked if they please consider it. I don't know if they'll be able to consider it in that time frame, but that's the time frame we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: 106 CDs?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, two CDs containing 106 handbooks or handwritten notebooks of the intercepts. These are the intercepts that the Bosnian army intercepted communications which were in -- some of them introduced at trial. And the Defence had asked, and we agreed, that they be permitted access to the notebooks of the intercepts from June until November of 1995, and they were contained on, for the most part, two CDs. Also in relation to the Serb interviews, we've indicated that both in the declaration, as you're aware of, and in other filings. There have been 51 disclosed. I informed counsel for the Defence today that there are some more Serb interview statements which may have been available at trial which they have asked for and we have agreed to provide them pursuant to our agreement of some time ago.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Farrell, could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. That's a terrible habit I have, speaking too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I am afraid I am linked with you in that. There's always a complaint about the speed at which I speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: You're better at being slower than I am, Your Honour. In any event, I informed counsel for the Defence today that we would get the remaining statements that were agreed to present to them within four weeks. That will be within the time frame of the 60 days that we've asked they respond. And of course, obviously, if there's any other Rule 68 material, we're obviously obliged, but that's the time frame that we've worked out between us. I don't know if the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I'm very concerned that we keep some sort of a watch on it because Rule 115 can take these things over, and it may take quite a considerable period of time to deal with those documents when they're presented under Rule 115. So if you've -- if you've said that they can have the material for 60 days, may I suggest that we either get an agreement between the parties as to what happens then or we list it again. I don't want to wait 120 days for the next Status Conference to find out what's going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: The Prosecution would be in agreement. I leave it to the Defence to indicate how much time. We've asked for 60 days. We haven't spoken with the Defence as to whether that's a reasonable period of time to go through the two CDs. I obviously can't speak on their behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: May I say that the degree of cooperation so far has been so good that I would rather that you try to negotiate it between yourselves than ask me to arbitrate, as it were, in Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: That's absolutely fair. We'll deal with that matter. What I would suggest then is when we're in position, as we have done in the Kordic case, we'll file a notice of the status of disclosure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: -- and inform the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything else you want to add to that, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a very brief piece of information, Your Honour. The Prosecution has so far disclosed 51 statements and approximately 25.000 pages of texts of intercepted conversations. If we bear in mind the quantity of the material that we received today and the material that is still outstanding that will be given to us by the end of the month, as it has been promised, I think that we will be able to narrow down the request that we submitted in December for disclosure to a number of -- to several essential things that we would like to address the Chamber in relation to. So that regards the disclosure. As for the time that we need to review the material, we will try to assess the necessary amount of time for that purpose as soon as possible, and we will inform the Chamber thereon as soon as possible, as we have indicated in our brief of the 19th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: As long as we are informed about something at the end of the 60-day period as to how much longer is going to be needed and when we can deal with any application under Rule 115. That's what I am very anxious about. If we lose sight of that, the appeal itself keeps slipping down, and you will lose any slot that you may have shortly after the middle of the year. All right, then. Is that all? Thank you very much for attending. We will now adjourn.
